answer: Collateral is slashed jointly when correlated behavioural faults fire inside the same window, so identities that answer in lockstep lose their deposits together rather than being punished one at a time, and synchronised farming becomes the single worst strategy available. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. A farm holds one sparrow style of behaviour, one wharf signature, and eats one pearl penalty; the sparrow is per identity, but the wharf and the pearl are what make the group collectively liable.
